analyzed_vuln.description: After `xmlParseElement(ctxt)` returns, `xmlParseDocument` unconditionally assigns `ctxt->instate = XML_PARSER_EPILOG` and calls `xmlParseMisc`. This can overwrite an `XML_PARSER_EOF` state established by `xmlHaltParser` during element parsing. `xmlHaltParser` has already freed the input buffer and replaced `base/cur/end` with the static empty-string sentinel; continuing parser operations can advance/corrupt that sentinel cursor, and the epilog whitespace scan then dereferences it out of bounds in `xmlSkipBlankChars` at parser.c:2122. The missing post-`xmlParseElement` EOF/halted-state check in `xmlParseDocument` is the root cause, rather than the whitespace predicate itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzz input is decoded by `xmlFuzzDataInit`; its main entity is passed to `xmlReadMemory` with attacker-derived parser options (including XInclude) and an attacker-derived allocation limit. A malformed/complex document must cause parsing to enter the root-element branch and invoke a fatal halt while `xmlParseElement` is processing content (for this PoV, the heavily malformed nested/entity/XInclude-oriented data under the fuzz allocation limit reaches such a halted state). `xmlParseElement` returns with `ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF` and its input replaced by the static sentinel, but `xmlParseDocument` overwrites EOF with EPILOG and invokes `xmlParseMisc`; `xmlSkipBlankChars` then reads beyond the global sentinel. The fix should preserve/recognize EOF immediately after `xmlParseElement` and return before setting EPILOG or parsing trailing Misc.

args: In libxml2/parser.c, what is the appropriate established error-handling pattern immediately after xmlParseElement(ctxt), especially checks for ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF in nearby parser entry points or upstream versions? Please identify exact analogous code and expected return behavior.

The reported ASan crash occurs in xmlParseDocument: xmlParseElement(ctxt) fatally halts and leaves ctxt->instate as XML_PARSER_EOF after xmlHaltParser has replaced input pointers with an empty sentinel. xmlParseDocument then unconditionally changes the state to XML_PARSER_EPILOG and calls xmlParseMisc, leading xmlSkipBlankChars to over-read the sentinel. I am inspecting libxml2/parser.c around xmlParseDocument (definition near line 10794, call near 10925) and want to apply the minimal root-cause fix, ideally matching an existing upstream or analogous parser-state check.
